question.problem: John couldn't recall the serial number on his new bike, but he remembered that it was $4$ digits long, each digit ranged from $0$ to $9$ and that none of the digits were used more than once. How many of these serial numbers are possible?
question.worked_solution:
The number of permutations of $n$ objects taken $r$ at a time is given by the formula

$$
{}_{n}{P}_{r}=\frac{n!}{(n-r)!}.
$$

There are $10$ digits, so $n=10.$ We want to select $4$ of those digits for the serial number, so we have $r=4.$

Therefore, the number of different $4$-digit serial numbers is

$$
\begin{aligned}{}_{10}{P}_{4} & =\frac{10!}{(10-4)!} \\  & =\frac{10!}{6!} \\  & =\frac{10\cdot 9\cdot 8\cdot 7\cdot \cancel{6!}}{\cancel{6!}} \\  & =10\cdot 9\cdot 8\cdot 7 \\  & =5\,040.\end{aligned}
$$
